questions.question: Which rollout plan should the team follow for the overlay change, given that the mini is headless and the Windows box is shared with the image server?

options.label: Mac first
options.description: Roll the overlay change out to the Mac machines first, including the headless mini, where it can be verified without disturbing anyone. Windows follows once the Mac results look good, so the image server is not touched until then.

options.label: Windows first
options.description: Roll out to the Windows box first so any conflict with the shared image server shows up early. The Macs, including the headless mini, follow after that result is known.

options.label: All three together
options.description: Deploy to the Macs, the headless mini and the Windows box in a single pass. This is the fastest route, but a problem would hit every machine at once and could interrupt the image server.

options.label: Hold until Monday
options.description: Delay the whole rollout until Monday, when the image server is less likely to be in use. This is the safest for shared resources but pushes the change back by days.

questions.question: Who should be told when the rollout finishes?

options.label: Only the lead
options.description: Send the completion notice to the lead alone.

options.label: The whole team
options.description: Send the completion notice to everyone on the team.

options.label: Nobody
options.description: Finish the rollout without sending any notification.
